myths.text: The name means "Navel (of the earth); the stone at Delphi regarded as the centre of the world" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Omphalós appears within the Greek tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Omphalós continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Greek tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Omphalós embodies navel, center, delphi in the Greek imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Omphalós is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Greek tradition.
